record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.context_brief: similarity to a symmetric nonnegative matrix
record.original_question: Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is both entrywise nonnegative and symmetric?

evidence.quote: both non- negative matrix and symmetric matrix

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $A \in M_n(\mathbb{R})$ be an entrywise nonnegative matrix (that is, every entry of $A$ is $\ge 0$). Determine whether there must always exist an invertible real matrix $P \in GL_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that the similar matrix $B = P^{-1} A P$ is simultaneously entrywise nonnegative and symmetric (i.e., $B_{ij} \ge 0$ for all $i,j$ and $B^T = B$). If not, characterize precisely those nonnegative matrices $A$ for which such an invertible real $P$ exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of when a nonnegative matrix is similar (via a real invertible matrix) to a symmetric nonnegative matrix is part of the symmetric nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem (SNIEP), which is well known to be open in general. Trivially, a nonnegative matrix with non-real spectrum cannot be similar to any real symmetric matrix, so the universal "must exist" version fails; but the structural classification remains unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: The symmetric nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem asks which lists of real numbers are spectra of symmetric nonnegative matrices; it remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetric NIEP is a long-standing open problem, indicating that the related similarity question is not fully resolved.
